scope: Private generated async resource canonical cancellation through maintained-C/Perry/maintained-C components on Linux; public guards retained
composition: Independent maintained-C provider defines the nominal resource type and can backpressure async entry.
The actual generated Perry guest imports that resource interface; public resource/async guards remain intact.
A maintained-C supervisor receives the same foreign instance and explicit root resource alias as Perry, then canonically cancels Perry calls.
A Rust persistent host supplies native observation and suspension gates with Turnloop-backed WASI providers; all 32 scenarios reuse the same Store within each run.

modes: instrumented production runtime with knobs off
instrumented production runtime with forced and verified evacuation
cases: Eight pre-start owned transfers: provider backpressure prevents argument consumption; cancellation drops the committed input exactly once.
Eight suspended borrowed calls: native child cancellation acknowledges before incoming borrow expiry; caller drops its owner and a late native completion is rejected.

Eight ready-result races: provider creates a new owner before releasing cancellation; observed runs finish successfully first, so the C caller drops the returned owner. This does not stand in for unclaimed-result coverage.

Eight deterministic unclaimed results: provider creates its result before cancellation, then returns it from its CANCEL callback. Perry must acknowledge cancellation, never publish to JS, and discard that canonical owner before acknowledging its caller.
All 32 calls retain an independent live sibling through acknowledgement. Each sibling later finishes normally; all gates empty and Store idle after every call.
80 distinct canonical resources are destroyed exactly once per complete run; per-call observers require relevant input/result destruction before acknowledgement.
